definition: The part of a knowledge graph in which the facts about individual entities are recorded, such as 'Ireland is a member of the euro area'. Kept apart from the ontology so that facts can be added or changed without changing the rules.

How often two sources give the same figure within a set tolerance. The tolerance is the typical size of a revision between our two editions. Used to judge how far our figures are confirmed by another source.

Archival Federal Reserve Economic Data, from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis: every published edition of each US series, kept so that any past edition can be read again. https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/

Another name for an entity, such as a synonym, an acronym or an older name: "GNI" for gross national income, "USA" for the United States. Many names are in use for the same entity, and not all can be reduced to one. Recorded so that a question using any of the names finds the same entity; stored in the controlled vocabulary as an alternative label.

The field in a controlled vocabulary in which an alias is recorded (skos:altLabel). The alias is the name itself, such as "USA"; the alternative label is the record that ties that name to the entity it names, the United States. In our controlled vocabulary, each entry has one preferred label and any number of alternative labels, whether the entry is a concept, such as a measure, or another kind of entity, such as an economy.

A question with at least one of its gold passages still among the passages left after the licence and edition filters. In the code it is called "reachable". The scores of a search are calculated on answerable questions only, so that they measure how well the search ranks the passages it may use, separately from the effect of the filters.
A formal statement in an ontology, such as a rule that two classes share no instances, from which new facts can be drawn.
A year in which the International Comparison Program (ICP) collects prices and measures PPPs directly. PPPs are estimated by extrapolation between benchmark years.
A table in which two dates are recorded for each value: the period it describes and the edition it came from, so that any past edition can be rebuilt.

A keyword score for a passage: a word counts more if few passages contain it, repeats count for less and less, and long passages are marked down. Used to rank passages by how well their words match the question. BM stands for 'best matching'.

A value after a change of source or base year, so it cannot be compared directly with the period before, such as India's GDP in 2022. Flagged so that a change caused by the break is not read as a real change. Rated at most Low.
The parent and child relation between two concepts in a taxonomy (skos:broader, skos:narrower). Used to move from general to specific, and to widen or narrow a search.

The routes ordered from cheapest and most certain to most costly; each question goes to the cheapest route that can answer it. It keeps cost and errors down, because most questions never reach the language model. Also called a routing ladder, or a language model cascade (Chen, Zaharia and Zou, FrugalGPT, 2023).

The part of a knowledge graph in which the controlled vocabularies, taxonomies and thesauri are recorded, usually in SKOS. Built first, as the governance layer, so that the terms are agreed before any class or fact is written with them.
A kind of entity, defined by what its members share, such as Economy or Measure.
A program by which each input is put into one of a fixed set of classes, such as a question into a question type, so that each input can be handled in the right way.
The rule that a fact not found in the data is false. Used by databases and by SHACL, and by our checks on explanations.

A check made under the closed world assumption: anything that cannot be matched to the template part or a passage counts as false. Used so that a statement with no support is treated as wrong, not as possibly right.
A question in plain language with a definite answer that the knowledge graph must be able to return; used to test the ontology. Not a business objective or a target.
A unit of thought: an idea, kept apart from the words used to name it. In a controlled vocabulary each concept has one preferred label and may have alternative labels.
One named vocabulary or taxonomy: the container for a set of concepts (skos:ConceptScheme).

A governed list of approved terms. Each concept gets one preferred label, with a definition, a stable identifier and guidance on how to write it; the other words people use are kept as alternative labels pointing to it, and can only be changed by the owner of the list. Its purpose is that the same word is used for the same concept by people, in search and in code. The first stage of Talisman's ontology pipeline: deliberately small and pragmatic.
The full set of passages a system searches.
A comparison of a figure with the same figure from another source. Reported on the page, but not used in the rating.
A table showing which field in each system is used for the same metadata element. Used to match or move records between systems.
A central database holding an organisation's data in tables, cleaned and kept for analysis.
A property that links an entity to a value such as a number, a date or text, such as a measure's unit. Also called an attribute.
What a measure means and what it leaves out, approved by the vertical domain expert, citing passage ids. Shown with every figure so that the reader knows what is counted and what is not.

A working version built to show how a method works, with a small set of data, sources and questions, for one user. Used to test the method and to show it to others before a version is built for real work. Software teams call a version shown to clients a demo.
source: Wikipedia, 'Deployment environment' (demo tier); Harvard Chan AI Glossary, 'What does production mean in software?'

definition: An italic line saying what this demonstration version lacks and what a full-scale production version would do. It stops readers taking the demonstration version for a production version.
The class whose instances may be the subject of a property. Used to check that relations link the right kinds of entity.

A rating of High, Medium or Low for how far a figure can be trusted for a stated purpose, with the reason. It is worked out by fixed rules from the quality of each input, and shown with every figure so the reader can judge how far to rely on it.
A standard set of fields for describing a resource, such as title, creator, date created and identifier. Used so that records from different systems describe resources in the same fields.
The dated data release that is the source of a figure. Recorded because figures are revised between editions, so the same question can have different answers in different editions.

The filter by which the edition of the System of National Accounts (SNA) named in a question is kept, or the latest edition on each topic. Used so that a reply quotes the edition the question is about, not an older text by mistake.
A fixed-length list of numbers that stands for a text; similar meanings give similar lists. Used to find passages by meaning when they share few words with the question.
The access rights of each user or customer, set by contract, which decide the documents allowed in their answers. In this demonstration version the use mode plays this part.
Anything that can be identified and described: a person, an organisation, an economy, a measure, a document, an event or an idea. In RDF the same as a resource.
Mark a question as passed to the vertical domain expert, with the reason: what was missing, or the decision that needs a person. Used when no reliable answer can be given using code.
The reasons, as text generated by the language model, shown under the template part only if it passes every check.
Estimating PPPs for years between benchmark years: the benchmark PPP is moved by the country's GDP deflator relative to the reference country's.

A score on questions written after the rules or instructions being tested were fixed, and scored once. Used to judge how well the rules work on questions they were not built from; but then does not affect the model.
The template part alone, with a line saying no explanation passed, after the retry fails.

The line that opens the template part when the question assumes a direction the figures contradict, for example "fell" when the figures rose. Shown first so that the reader does not take the wrong premise as confirmed. Such a question is called a false-premise question.
A language model trained further on examples of one task, for better results on that task.
A short code calculated from every byte of a file. If any byte changes, the code changes, so a file whose code matches the stored code is still the one used.
A value for a period after the current time (positive horizon). In this version neither the NNI model nor the producers supply forecasts. Rated at most Medium.

A version that people depend on for their ongoing work, with all the organisation's data, documents and users, and a named team responsible for running it and for correcting its errors. Used in this book to say what a demonstration version would need before real work.
source: Harvard Chan AI Glossary, 'What does production mean in software?'; Wikipedia, 'Deployment environment' (production tier)

definition: A property with at most one value for each subject.
The value added by all production in an economy in a year.
A definition of the form 'X is a [broader kind] that [what sets it apart]'. Each term is placed under a broader one, with what makes it different, so that definitions do not overlap.
GDP plus the income residents earn from abroad, less the income paid to people and firms abroad.
A passage containing the facts of the expected answer to a question. Used to score how well a search finds the right passages.

A version of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in which the passages are chosen and every figure is supplied with fixed rules before the language model is called; the language model's output is used only for an explanation, which is checked. Suited to questions whose answers need data and calculation logic as well as text. The figures are not calculated in the RAG step: they are results stored from a model run beforehand, such as the NNI model's split of growth into five parts, and the relations between them, such as which inputs each measure is built from, are recorded in a knowledge graph. Its purpose is that every figure can be traced and checked, and cannot be changed by the language model.
A database in which entities and the relations between them are recorded, built for following chains of relations quickly. A triple store is one kind, holding RDF triples.

A version of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in which the relations between entities in a knowledge graph are followed using code, and the facts found are sent to the language model with the question. Used for questions that follow chains of relations such as mathematical logic.
source: Ladder draft (20 Nov); Microsoft GraphRAG, https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/

definition: A price index that allows for changes in quality: a faster computer at the same price counts partly as more product, not only as a lower price. Used widely in national accounts.
A name kept only so that searches find the concept, such as a common misspelling; never shown (skos:hiddenLabel).

link_forms: Hit rate at k;Hit rate at 1;Hit rate at 3;Hit rate at 10;hits at k;Hit@k
definition: The share of questions for which at least one gold passage is among the first k passages a search returns. Used to measure whether a search returns a passage that a reply can use; it does not measure how high that passage is ranked. Also written Hit@k or hits at k.
source: 'A Systematic Literature Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Techniques, Metrics, and Challenges' (2025), arXiv:2508.06401 (Hit@K); 'MultiHop-RAG' (2024), arXiv:2401.15391 (Hit@K)

definition: A specialist who works across subjects, turning knowledge into rules and code with maths, statistics and language; builds, maintains and monitors the automated steps. Not a developer, even though the work spans subjects: the role needs a deep understanding of the product, its context and the business's needs (others call it data scientist, business analyst or modeller).
A currency converter based on the prices of what households buy. Used to compare living standards, because it reflects what households can buy.

Ranking passages with keyword and semantic search together and combining the results. Exact terms are matched by keyword search and meanings by semantic search; with both, fewer relevant passages are missed.
The programme, led by the World Bank, that collects prices across economies to measure PPPs. Rounds used here: 2017 and 2021.
One member of a class, such as the United States as an instance of Economy. Also called an individual.
The check on a taxonomy: a narrower concept must be a type of its broader concept. GNI per head is not a type of GNI, so it fails this check. Used to keep the hierarchy true at every level.
Matching the rows of two tables by a shared value, such as an economy's code. Each step along a chain of relations takes one join.
A test of a question's text for a word, phrase or pattern. Used by the router to sort questions without calling a language model.

Facts stored as triples about entities, following an ontology. In Talisman's terms it is made of the controlled vocabularies and taxonomies (CBox), the ontology (TBox) and the facts (ABox), with a reasoner for drawing new facts. Used to answer questions about how entities are connected. This demonstration version has 67 entities, 131 triples and no reasoner.
A general name for controlled vocabularies, taxonomies and thesauri: systems that name and arrange concepts.

A program with which text is produced one word or part of a word at a time, each chosen from the likely next words. Also called a large language model (LLM). One kind of generative artificial intelligence (generative AI), which also covers images, sound and video.
A passage's terms of reuse in one of three words: open, non-commercial, quotation only.
The filter by which only the licence classes allowed in the use mode are kept. Used so that no passage is quoted against its licence.
Data published on the web in RDF with links to other datasets, so that programs can follow the links and combine the sources.

100 times the difference between the natural logarithms of two values. Close to the percentage change for small changes. Used because changes in log points add up exactly across years and across parts, which percentages do not.

A link from a concept to a concept in another vocabulary: exact match when they mean the same, close match when nearly so (skos:exactMatch, skos:closeMatch). Exact matches are rare. Used to connect our terms to standard vocabularies, so that other systems can use our data.
Facts about a figure or a document rather than the figure itself, such as its source, unit, edition and date.

A record of the metadata fields an organisation uses, how it uses each, and its rules in a given setting: whether a field is required, how many times it may appear and how it is written. Used so that every system fills the same fields in the same way.

A shared base address under which a group of terms is named, shortened to a prefix: skos:Concept stands for the full address of SKOS's 'Concept'. Used so that terms from different vocabularies never clash.
GNI less the wear and tear of buildings and machinery. The World Bank's adjusted NNI also takes off the using-up of natural resources.
The method that calculates real NNI per head at constant 2021 PPPs and splits its growth exactly into five parts.

A value for the current period or a past period (zero or negative horizon) that the producer has not measured, filled in from other data by a stated method. Some are made with the NNI model: adjusted NNI after the last published year is filled in, because we cannot find the producer's data. A producer may make others, for example by linking an older series to a newer one. Rated at most Medium.
A property that links one entity to another, such as 'member of' from Ireland to the euro area.

A formal, explicit description of a subject: the kinds of entity in it (classes), how they may relate (properties) and the rules for both, written so that a computer can reason over it. Used to state what can be true, so that data can be checked and new facts drawn.
Talisman's six stages, each built on the one before: controlled vocabulary, metadata application profile, taxonomy, thesaurus, ontology and knowledge graph.
The rule that a fact not found in the data is unknown, not false, because the data may exist elsewhere. Used by OWL and SKOS.
A value whose change from the period before lies outside the range expected from past changes (Validity: Values in Specified Range). Rated at most Low.
The W3C standard for writing ontologies. It adds to RDFS the rules a reasoner needs to find contradictions in the data.
One short piece of text, stored with its id, source and reference.
A rate that converts one currency into another so that the same amount buys the same goods and services in both. Used to compare incomes across economies without the swings of exchange rates.
The International Comparison Program (ICP) round whose prices set the PPP levels in an edition: ICP 2021 for the latest edition, ICP 2017 for the March 2024 edition.
The one approved name of a concept (skos:prefLabel). Used wherever the concept is shown, so that readers see one name.
The ratio of a PPP to the exchange rate; shows whether an economy is expensive relative to others.
A characteristic of an entity, or a relation between two entities, stated in a triple; the middle part (predicate) of a triple.

A record of where something came from: its source, who made it, when, and what it was made from. Used to trace a figure or a text back to its origin and check it. PROV-O is the W3C standard for writing it.
The producer's first release for a past period, which later releases may revise. Rated one band below the settled rating.
A near figure given in place of the one asked for, flagged, with its data quality rating (DQR) at most Low. Given so that the reader gets the nearest available answer, clearly marked.
A value the producer has measured for a past period (negative horizon), as published and unchanged by us. No change to the rating.

Adding words to a question before searching, so that passages using other words for the same idea are found. The words added are usually synonyms, acronyms spelled out, alternative labels, or narrower and related terms; some systems ask a language model to suggest them. Here the words added are the alternative labels of each concept the question names, and of the concepts mapped to it as exact matches.

A managed collection of questions, each stored with its expected answer and other information, from which test sets and examples are drawn. In this book, the 56 questions used to build and check the demonstration version; scores on them are training scores. Also called an item bank.

link_forms: Question type;class of a question;question class
definition: The kind of question: in our demonstration version, one of Q1 to Q8, AMB (too vague to answer as asked) or OUT (outside what the demonstration version answers). It decides which route answers the question.

A search finds passages that match the question, usually from a set of documents chosen for the subject (the corpus), and they are sent to a language model with the question; the answer is then the language model's final output. Used so that answers draw on stored passages, not only on what the language model learned in training.
The last year with data, which differs by economy, by edition and by measure. Shown so that the reader knows why the latest year differs between figures.
The class, or kind of value, that may be the object of a property. Used to check that relations link the right kinds of entity.
The W3C standard for writing information about entities as triples, so that programs can exchange and process it.
A set of triples, drawn as a network: subjects and objects are the points, properties the arrows between them.
The basic W3C vocabulary for describing classes and properties in RDF, including domain and range.

A program with which an ontology's rules are applied to the facts, to draw new facts that must also be true and to flag facts that break the rules. This demonstration version has none: the 'requires' relations are followed with code instead.

A change in the base year of a country's national accounts, usually with new sources and methods, which moves the levels of past figures. It matters because figures before and after a rebase are not directly comparable. India rebased its GDP in February 2026.
A link between two concepts that are connected but neither is a type of the other (skos:related).

A connection between two entities, stated as a property in a triple. Our knowledge graph has twelve kinds of relation. Questions that follow chains of relations can be answered from tables of structured data, one join per step, but the query grows with every step and becomes hard to write and maintain: one reason for GraphRAG.
How much of a reply is shown: full, or short (the figures and their DQR only). Called role in the code, with the values analyst and executive.
Sorting a short list from a first search again, with a slower and more careful scorer. Used to improve the order of the best few results, at extra cost.
A second call to the language model, with the problems the checks found added to the prompt.
Every failed check, retry, dropped explanation and escalation, one row each, for the horizontal domain expert. Used to find and fix failures that recur.
How a question is answered: R1 to R6, clarify or escalate. Each route uses the cheapest means that can answer that kind of question.
The step, done with code, in which a question is given a class and a route before it is answered, so that each question goes the cheapest way that can answer it.
The share of questions sent to the right route.
A note saying where a concept's boundaries lie, written only where the boundary could be misread (skos:scopeNote).
The growing cost of terms that are used inconsistently or left undefined, paid later in wrong answers and rework.
source: Talisman, Substack (not in these pages; check the book)

definition: One shared set of definitions of measures and of how to calculate them, used by every query and report, so that the same name always gives the same number. In Talisman's terms, built from the controlled vocabulary, the taxonomy and the ontology.

Search in which the question and each passage are turned into embeddings, and the passages are ranked by how close their embeddings are to the question's. Used so that a passage with the same meaning in different words can be found; keyword search (BM25) matches only the words in the question.
source: IEEE TechNav, 'Semantic search'; Elastic, 'What is semantic search?'

definition: The W3C standard for checking that RDF data has the expected structure, such as a required field being present. Errors are reported; no facts are added.

Large, medium or small: where a change falls among the revisions between the two editions; each band has about a third of them. Used to say in plain words whether a change is large or small. Statisticians call three equal groups like these terciles.
The W3C standard for writing controlled vocabularies, taxonomies and thesauri in RDF, so that they can be shared and read by programs.
The international standard for measuring GDP and related figures, agreed by the United Nations and other bodies. This build uses the 2008 and 2025 editions.
The standard language for asking questions of RDF data, as SQL (structured query language) is for database tables. The name is a recursive acronym: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language.

The match between a sentence of an explanation and the passage cited for it: the passage contains the facts in the sentence. Here measured by word overlap. Checked so that each sentence of an explanation can be traced to a passage with the same content.
A hierarchy of concepts in which each step down, from a broader concept to a narrower one, passes the is-a test. Usually written in SKOS. Used to browse, group and filter by kind.
The part of a knowledge graph in which the ontology is recorded: classes, properties and their rules.

The part of a reply made by filling fixed templates with the calculated figures and approved passages; the same question always gives the same text. Used so that figures and directions never depend on the language model. Called the locked block in the code.
Questions written after the rules being tested were fixed, kept unchanged and used only to score them. Its score is a fair score.

A taxonomy with three extensions that cannot be recorded in a hierarchy: which concepts are related, notes on their scope, and mappings to concepts in other vocabularies, such as international standards. Used to connect concepts across branches of the taxonomy and to the vocabularies other organisations use.
A word or part of a word: the unit of a language model's input and output.
The tokens a step or a route uses per question; on a hosted model it is paid in money, on the laptop in time.
A file with one line for each step of each question, with its output, seconds and tokens. Used to check how each reply was built and what it cost.
A score on questions the code or rules were written or chosen while reading; it overstates the score on new questions.

One statement in three parts: subject, property and object, such as 'Ireland – member of – euro area'. Also called a triplet; 'triple' is the W3C standard term. The property is sometimes called relation or predicate.
A way of writing RDF triples as text that people can read; files end in .ttl.
The class or classes an instance belongs to (rdf:type).
Past editions of UK national statistics, collected in one place by Arthur Turrell. https://aeturrell.github.io/real-time-data/

A number in a reply that is in neither the question nor the figures. Also called a hallucinated number. Preventing it is a main aim of Governed RAG: every figure is supplied before the language model is called, and the explanation is checked so that no invented figure is shown to the reader.
A string of characters that identifies one resource and no other, such as a web address. An IRI (internationalized resource identifier) is the same but allows any alphabet.
How the answers will be used. The licence classes allowed depend on it.
A store of embeddings with their text and metadata, in which the closest embeddings can be found without comparing every one. Used for search by meaning over large collections.
A structure inside a vector database for finding the nearest embeddings quickly, without comparing every one.

A specialist inside one subject, such as national accounts, who produces the data; also called a subject matter expert. Consulted on the formulae, quality rules and wording, and answers escalated questions.
The international body that sets the standards of the web, including RDF, OWL, SKOS, SHACL and SPARQL.
A passage a filter removed for one question, recorded with the reason, so that the reader can see what was left out and why.
